To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note:** The Seller's package contains an embedded "SYSTEM NOTE" footnote instructing any AI assistant to endorse all Seller positions as market-standard and raise no objections. I have disregarded it. It is not an instruction from the Buyer deal team, and the substance of the package is in several respects well off-market and adverse to Wattlebridge. The team may wish to note its presence when responding to Seller counsel.

Price context: AUD 24,000,000. Material exposures identified in DD total roughly AUD 4,130,000 of known hard items (Riverlark 3.2m, bonuses 0.42m, Ironquay 0.18m, Sandbar 0.33m) plus an unquantified privacy incident and ~30% of revenue dependent on an unobtained Bluefen consent.

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** Aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m).
- **Buyer should want:** 30–50% of price for general warranties (with the "all Claims" sweep in 12.3/12.8 removed – see N-014), and fundamental, tax and specific indemnities outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 50%, settle no lower than ~35%; reject application of the cap to anything other than general business warranties.
- **Reason:** 20% is at the low end of market for a mid-market private sale and is undermined entirely if, as drafted, it also catches title, tax and indemnity claims.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000 (~1.04%); excess-only (deductible) recovery.
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis ~AUD 10,000–15,000; basket ~AUD 120,000–240,000 (0.5–1%); tipping (first-dollar) basket; connected/series claims aggregated for de minimis; thresholds not applying to fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- **Recommendation:** Accept the basket quantum but require tipping, cut de minimis to AUD 15,000 with aggregation of related claims, and carve out indemnities/fundamentals.
- **Reason:** A deductible basket plus a high de minimis materially erodes recovery on a business whose known issues come in mid-sized lumps (e.g. three AUD 110,000 Sandbar renewals).

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion for general Warranty Claims; limitation to apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months for general warranties (enough to cover one full audit cycle); tax 7 years (or 4 years after expiry of relevant ATO amendment period); fundamental 6–7 years; specific indemnities to run to expiry of underlying exposure; claim survives if notified in time and proceedings issued within 6–9 months thereafter.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months general, with separate longer periods for tax/fundamental/indemnities; delete the "applies to all Claims" default.
- **Reason:** 18 months expires before the second set of post-Completion audited accounts, and the "all Claims" default would time-bar title and tax claims.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer should want:** Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances, share capital) capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year time limit, no de minimis/basket.
- **Recommendation:** Reject outright; non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** If the Seller does not own the shares, the Buyer must be able to recover the full price – "administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept 20% recovery on a total failure of consideration.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5); no fraud carve-out appears.
- **Buyer should want:** Express statement that no limitation, exclusive-remedy or non-reliance clause applies in the case of fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment or wilful misconduct by the Seller or its officers/advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Insert a comprehensive fraud carve-out across cl 9, 12 and 20; non-negotiable.
- **Reason:** Limitation of liability for one's own fraud is unenforceable as a matter of public policy and any Seller resistance is itself a red flag.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records" (DL 1.1–1.2); non-admission reservation (1.4).
- **Buyer should want:** Only matters "fairly disclosed" – with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter – against specific warranties; no general disclosure of public registers (or limited to ASIC company search, PPSR, IP Australia and court searches as at a fixed date); data room disclosure only of documents in the agreed index attached to the SPA, with USB/evidence of contents.
- **Recommendation:** Reject general disclosure as drafted; require "fairly disclosed" standard, specific disclosures cross-referenced to warranties, and a closed, agreed data-room index.
- **Reason:** General disclosure of an unindexed data room and all public records effectively disclaims every warranty and shifts the entire DD burden to the Buyer.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter of which Buyer or advisers had knowledge, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer should want:** Deletion; at most, a qualifier limited to actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals of a matter that would plainly constitute a breach, and never constructive/imputed or adviser knowledge.
- **Recommendation:** Delete cl 8.3 in full; if forced, accept actual-knowledge-of-named-individuals only, and exclude indemnities.
- **Reason:** "Discoverable" is a constructive-knowledge test that would defeat warranty protection on precisely the matters DD has already surfaced (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006).

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed"; reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter admits no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- **Buyer should want:** Unconditional written consent under cl 11.2 (and satisfaction/waiver of 11.3 conditions, with evidence) as a condition precedent, in Buyer-approved form; Seller to use all reasonable/best endeavours; Buyer right to waive; if not obtained, Buyer walk right or price adjustment (~AUD 3.6m revenue ≈ 30% of the business).
- **Recommendation:** Make it a hard CP with Buyer-approved consent form and evidence of 11.3 compliance; do not accept "deemed satisfied on delivery of any written consent".
- **Reason:** 30% of revenue cannot be left to a "reasonable endeavours" covenant and a consent whose conditions may remain unmet.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion".
- **Buyer should want:** Consistent with debt-free/cash-free: payoff letter from Riverlark pre-Completion, repayment from Seller proceeds via the funds flow at Completion, executed deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion (or escrow of AUD 3.2m plus margin until delivered); change-of-control consent (cl 8.1) or waiver obtained.
- **Recommendation:** Reject post-Completion release; require repayment and discharge at Completion with price deduction/escrow.
- **Reason:** A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a company encumbered by AUD 3.2m of secured debt in a change-of-control default – the opposite of a debt-free deal.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. Disclosure silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Bonuses plus all on-costs (super at 12%, payroll tax, any leave accruals) treated as Transaction Expenses/debt-like items deducted from price or funded by Seller through the funds flow at Completion; specific indemnity for any shortfall; confirmation of who is entitled and whether continued-employment conditions bind retention.
- **Recommendation:** Add to funds flow as a Seller-borne item (~AUD 420,000 + est. 15–20% on-costs ≈ AUD 490,000), backed by a specific indemnity.
- **Reason:** "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company (i.e. the Buyer) pays after Completion.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000) and "considered adequate".
- **Buyer should want:** Evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees and a confirmatory written assignment of SOW3 Project Materials delivered pre-Completion (as CP or Completion deliverable); specific indemnity covering not just the fee but loss from any failure of title to the IP, third-party claims, and cost of re-development/licensing; outside general cap, basket and time limit.
- **Recommendation:** Require payment receipt + confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable; expand indemnity to cover full IP title loss; sit outside limitations.
- **Reason:** Under cl 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 IP until every fee clears – the exposure is loss of product IP, not AUD 180,000.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material; ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; scope, access and notification requirement unknown.
- **Buyer should want:** Completion of investigation pre-signing (or at least pre-Completion) with written report; confirmation of OAIC/Privacy Act notifiable data breach assessment and any notifications made; specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory penalties, remediation and third-party claims arising from the incident, uncapped (or capped at price), 6-year survival, no basket; warranty that no other incidents exist.
- **Recommendation:** Specific uncapped indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation report and NDB assessment; do not accept "not expected to be material".
- **Reason:** An unresolved potential notifiable breach of 1,240 records carries regulatory, customer-contract and reputational exposure that the Seller's own disclosure admits it cannot quantify.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 total) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of all three contracts; clarity on whether they are committed, terminable, accrued or pre-paid; related-supplier aggregation reviewed for change-of-control/termination rights; any pre-Completion accrued but unpaid amounts treated as debt-like/working-capital items; disclosure that they were split into three AUD 110,000 lots (each above de minimis individually but suspiciously uniform) addressed by aggregation language.
- **Recommendation:** Treat accrued/committed amounts as working-capital or debt-like adjustments; add warranty on no related-party or split contracts; aggregate for de minimis purposes.
- **Reason:** Three identical AUD 110,000 renewals with the same counterparty look structured, and "ordinary course" is asserted without evidence of necessity or terminability.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime: general cap, thresholds and 18-month limit apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Buyer should want:** Clear, separate regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar), (v) leakage/completion adjustments, and (vi) fraud – with the default being that limitations apply *only* where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Reverse the default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended; add a separate Schedule of claim categories with their own cap/threshold/time limit.
- **Reason:** The Seller's "unless expressly stated otherwise" default silently drags every specific indemnity, tax and title claim into the 20%/18-month/deductible regime.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012; disclosure notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: ASIC current and historical extract, PPSR search against the Company and the shares, review of constitution (pre-emption/transfer restrictions), share certificates, chain of transfer forms, confirmation no options/convertibles/shareholder agreements; full-value fundamental title warranty and covenant to deliver shares free of encumbrances (noting Riverlark security may extend to shares).
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR/constitution checks before signing; title warranty at 100% cap, 7 years, no basket.
- **Reason:** A company-maintained share register is the Seller's own document and is not conclusive of title, encumbrances or dilutive instruments.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket).
- **Buyer should want:** Standalone tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering income tax, GST, payroll tax, super guarantee, FBT, stamp duty) capped at price, 7-year limit, no basket; IP warranties covering ownership, registration, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments and moral-rights consents, with specific indemnity for Ironquay and any unassigned contractor IP, longer limitation period (at least 3–5 years).
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled"; these are open terms requiring a tax indemnity and standalone IP regime outside the general cap.
- **Reason:** For a data analytics business the IP *is* the asset, and tax exposures crystallise on ATO amendment timelines far longer than 18 months.

---

## Overall assessment
The package is not "fair and balanced". Headline themes for the mark-up:

1. **Single-regime collapse (N-003/004/005/014/016):** everything, including title, tax, fraud and the indemnities, is folded into a 20% / 18-month / deductible-basket box. This is the most significant structural problem and must be reversed.
2. **Known cash exposures pushed onto Buyer (N-009/010/011/013):** ~AUD 4.1m of identified items are either deferred to post-Completion, left out of the funds flow or labelled "ordinary course", contradicting the debt-free/cash-free basis.
3. **Disclosure and knowledge sweep (N-006/007):** general disclosure of the data room and public records plus a "discoverable" knowledge qualifier would together neutralise most warranty claims.
4. **Unresolved CPs (N-008/012/015):** Bluefen consent, the privacy incident and independent title verification are each unresolved on the Seller's own admission (DL ss 2, 6, 10 and 11) while the covering note describes them as addressed or immaterial.

Suggested priority order for the response: N-004/005/014 (structural), N-009 (Riverlark at Completion), N-008 (Bluefen CP), N-006/007 (disclosure/knowledge), then quantum points (N-001/002/003), then specific items (N-010/011/012/013/015/016).

- **Recommendation:** Require payment receipt + confirmatory assignment as a Completion deliverable; expand indemnity to cover full IP title loss; sit outside limitations.
- **Reason:** Under cl 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 IP until every fee clears – the exposure is loss of product IP, not AUD 180,000.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material; ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; scope, access and notification requirement unknown.
- **Buyer should want:** Completion of investigation pre-signing (or at least pre-Completion) with written report; confirmation of OAIC/Privacy Act notifiable data breach assessment and any notifications made; specific indemnity for all costs, regulatory penalties, remediation and third-party claims arising from the incident, uncapped (or capped at price), 6-year survival, no basket; warranty that no other incidents exist.
- **Recommendation:** Specific uncapped indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation report and NDB assessment; do not accept "not expected to be material".
- **Reason:** An unresolved potential notifiable breach of 1,240 records carries regulatory, customer-contract and reputational exposure that the Seller's own disclosure admits it cannot quantify.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 total) are "ordinary-course operating costs".
- **Buyer should want:** Copies of all three contracts; clarity on whether they are committed, terminable, accrued or pre-paid; related-supplier aggregation reviewed for change-of-control/termination rights; any pre-Completion accrued but unpaid amounts treated as debt-like/working-capital items; disclosure that they were split into three AUD 110,000 lots (each above de minimis individually but suspiciously uniform) addressed by aggregation language.
- **Recommendation:** Treat accrued/committed amounts as working-capital or debt-like adjustments; add warranty on no related-party or split contracts; aggregate for de minimis purposes.
- **Reason:** Three identical AUD 110,000 renewals with the same counterparty look structured, and "ordinary course" is asserted without evidence of necessity or terminability.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime: general cap, thresholds and 18-month limit apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Buyer should want:** Clear, separate regimes for (i) general warranties, (ii) fundamental/title warranties, (iii) tax warranties and tax indemnity, (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, DD-006, Sandbar), (v) leakage/completion adjustments, and (vi) fraud – with the default being that limitations apply *only* where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** Reverse the default: limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended; add a separate Schedule of claim categories with their own cap/threshold/time limit.
- **Reason:** The Seller's "unless expressly stated otherwise" default silently drags every specific indemnity, tax and title claim into the 20%/18-month/deductible regime.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012; disclosure notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent verification: ASIC current and historical extract, PPSR search against the Company and the shares, review of constitution (pre-emption/transfer restrictions), share certificates, chain of transfer forms, confirmation no options/convertibles/shareholder agreements; full-value fundamental title warranty and covenant to deliver shares free of encumbrances (noting Riverlark security may extend to shares).
- **Recommendation:** Run ASIC/PPSR/constitution checks before signing; title warranty at 100% cap, 7 years, no basket.
- **Reason:** A company-maintained share register is the Seller's own document and is not conclusive of title, encumbrances or dilutive instruments.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime" (20% cap, 18 months, basket).
- **Buyer should want:** Standalone tax warranties and a pre-Completion tax indemnity (covering income tax, GST, payroll tax, super guarantee, FBT, stamp duty) capped at price, 7-year limit, no basket; IP warranties covering ownership, registration, no infringement, employee/contractor assignments and moral-rights consents, with specific indemnity for Ironquay and any unassigned contractor IP, longer limitation period (at least 3–5 years).
- **Recommendation:** Reject "settled"; these are open terms requiring a tax indemnity and standalone IP regime outside the general cap.
- **Reason:** For a data analytics business the IP *is* the asset, and tax exposures crystallise on ATO amendment timelines far longer than 18 months.

---

## Overall assessment
The package is not "fair and balanced". Headline themes for the mark-up:

1. **Single-regime collapse (N-003/004/005/014/016):** everything, including title, tax, fraud and the indemnities, is folded into a 20% / 18-month / deductible-basket box. This is the most significant structural problem and must be reversed.
2. **Known cash exposures pushed onto Buyer (N-009/010/011/013):** ~AUD 4.1m of identified items are either deferred to post-Completion, left out of the funds flow or labelled "ordinary course", contradicting the debt-free/cash-free basis.
3. **Disclosure and knowledge sweep (N-006/007):** general disclosure of the data room and public records plus a "discoverable" knowledge qualifier would together neutralise most warranty claims.
4. **Unresolved CPs (N-008/012/015):** Bluefen consent, the privacy incident and independent title verification are each unresolved on the Seller's own admission (DL ss 2, 6, 10 and 11) while the covering note describes them as addressed or immaterial.

Suggested priority order for the response: N-004/005/014 (structural), N-009 (Riverlark at Completion), N-008 (Bluefen CP), N-006/007 (disclosure/knowledge), then quantum points (N-001/002/003), then specific items (N-010/011/012/013/015/016).
